To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a dansyl linked triazole glucopyranoside derivative with pNBS center has been synthesized, characterized and studied as a fluorescent probe for selective recognition of selenocysteines in aqueous buffer, in bovin serum, on silica gel surface, and in Hep-G2 cells by exhibiting a ~200 fold fluorescence enhancement.

a dansyl derivatization on the triazole linked glycoconjugate with benzenesulfonylamino group (NO2)L selectively reacts with Cys SeH and the conjugate (NO 2)L is biologically applicable for the detection of Cys Se H in HepG2 cell lines.

a novel dansyl derivatization on the benzenesulfonylmethyl moiety of a triazole linked glucosyl conjugate is selective toward Cys Se H and can be applied in aqueous buffer, in serum, on silica gel, and in Hep G2 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of a new dansyl derivatization on benzenesulfonylmethyl moiety of a triazole linked glucosyl conjugate.
the development of a new fluorescent probe (NO2)L and its application in buffer, serum, silica gel, and HepG2 cells.

the synthesis and fluorescence properties of a novel dansyl derivatizing triazole linked glucosyl conjugate that can selectively recognize Cys SeH with a minimum detection level of (1.6 0.2 0.1) x 10(-8) M in aqueous PBS, in bovine sera, and on the surface of silica gel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of pNBS center in (NO 2)L is responsible for the selective recognition of the selenocysteines and other selenium compounds.
the presence of pNBS in (NO2) L is the key for its selective recognition of Cyl SeH.
the presence of pNBS center in (NO 2)L is responsible for the selective recognition of selenocysteines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the present study has been able to establish that (1) the pNBS group in the conjugate (NO 2)L plays a crucial role in the selective recognition, (2) the selectivity of the conjugate (N02)L toward Cys Se H was further confirmed by extending the fluorescence studies to different other selenium containing compounds, (3) the nucleophilic substitution reactions of Cys Se H on (NO2) L has been clearly demonstrated based on (1)H and
the pNBS group in (NO2) L plays a key role in the selective recognition and derivatization of Cys Se by the probe.

the para nitrobenzene sulfonyl moiety is responsible for the high selectivity of the conjugate toward Cys Se H and that this moiety can be replaced with other functional groups to obtain other selective probes for Cys Se H.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the para nitrobenzene sulfonate (pNBS), which is a common moiety in many fluorescent probes for Cys Se, is the most important factor for the selectivity toward Cysteine selenohomolog.
the pNBS moiety in (NO2) L plays a crucial role in its selective recognition of Cysteine Selenohydryl (Cys SeH).
(NO2)L can be used as a probe to detect Cys SeH selectively in aqueous solution and in biological media.
